NVDA.headline: Mixed AI-sector news as neocloud debut and German investments emerge
NVDA.summary: Shares closed at 217.09 USD, up 1.38% today but down 4.53% over one month, and sit within a 52-week range of 164.27–243.37. Reports say a newly listed neocloud had a weak debut, reigniting AI bubble concerns, while Nvidia plans to back four German AI startups as part of a near-$10 billion European push, with undisclosed investment amounts. Broader commentary on whether the AI investment boom is turning also weighs on sentiment.

MSFT.headline: UK regulator proposes market designation; AI spending cuts reported
MSFT.summary: Shares were at 533.52 USD, up 0.84% today and 6.36% over one month, though only 1.89% over one year and close to the 52-week high of 553.72. The UK Competition and Markets Authority is proposing Strategic Market Status for Microsoft in business software, which could lead to changes in bundling, licensing and interoperability. Reports say some businesses cut AI spending on third-party tools, including Microsoft's cut to internal Claude spending, and Microsoft withdrew from an Essex data-centre project.

AAPL.headline: Privacy crackdown, iPhone purchase limits and $5.7bn patent verdict
AAPL.summary: Shares were at 342.94 USD, down 0.15% today, up 1.17% over one month and near the upper end of their 52-week range of 243.42–348.15. Apple reportedly set a two-unit purchase limit for the iPhone Duo in the US and India, which Apple has not officially announced. Taction won a record $5.7 billion patent verdict against Apple, which Apple is challenging, and Taction has asked for more damages. Apple is also reported to be preparing a product event on 28 October.

GOOGL.headline: Anthropic stake reports, teen app safety findings and Android Auto plans
GOOGL.summary: Shares closed at 344.18 USD, up 1.05% today but down 3.04% over one month, within a 52-week range of 244.15–408.61. Reports that former Google CEO Eric Schmidt holds about a 1% stake in Anthropic are unverified and not commented on by the parties. A Tech Transparency Project report found nudify apps were accessible to test teen accounts despite parental controls, and Apple and Google said they took action. No major company-specific price driver is reported beyond these stories.

AMZN.headline: Shares jump nearly 5% with no company-specific news in the feed
AMZN.summary: Shares closed at 262.45 USD, up 4.98% today, up 1.55% over one month and 17.06% over one year, within a 52-week range of 196–287.2. The feed contains no Amazon-specific cause for the move. Related items are an unverified report on the God of War series and Anthropic's plan to set aside 5% of its shares for a public benefit fund, though Anthropic is privately held.

META.headline: Claude-linked account error, AI spending cuts and WhatsApp browser test
META.summary: Shares were at 705.44 USD, down 0.55% today and 4.83% over one month, within a 52-week range of 520.26–779.82. Meta said an automated security system, linked to a Claude AI tool, wrongly suspended the No Kings Coalition Instagram account. Reports say Meta halved its Claude Code users, and WhatsApp may extend its in-app browser to all links, with no timeline. Meta's results are due on Wednesday.

AVGO.headline: No major news; shares up 1.78% today
AVGO.summary: There is no major news right now for Broadcom. The shares are up 1.78% today at 334.59 USD, but are down 7.74% over one month and 5.52% over one year. The stock trades within a 52-week range of 289.96 to 495.

TSLA.headline: Merger speculation and robotaxi expansion news; shares up 3.76%
TSLA.summary: Tesla shares rose 3.76% today to 368.06 USD, though they remain down 1.93% over one month and 15.14% over one year. Reports of Tesla and SpaceXAI activity on X have fuelled merger speculation, but nothing has been confirmed and no official statement was given. Tesla's results are due on Wednesday, alongside Meta's, and a broader market recovery was reported on Monday.

TSM.headline: Chip sector pressure, Samsung-TSMC report and China growth data
TSM.summary: Shares were at 420.22 USD, up 1.84% today but down 5.6% over one month, within a 52-week range of 266.82–487.47. BTIG warns of a prolonged semiconductor decline and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 11.4% in the week. A Benzinga headline reports Samsung has reportedly turned to TSMC for Nvidia's next-generation memory, which is unconfirmed. China's Q3 growth of 4.5% was helped by AI-related chip exports.

SPCX.headline: India minister says AI will support space missions
SPCX.summary: Shares closed at 147.96 USD, up 1.32% today, down 2.56% over one month and 8.07% over one year, within a 52-week range of 104.83–225.64. The only news is an interview in which India's science and technology minister said AI would strengthen India's space missions. The remark is a policy statement with no figures or timelines and no direct company link.
